title: Staging Recovery live Worker provider evidence and ingress revalidation

phases.objective: Bind Staging Recovery certification to provider-observed Cloudflare Worker provenance and a fresh Activation Gateway ingress identity without extending mutation authority.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Capture the deployed Staging Worker provider identity, bind it to a fresh readiness response, execute the local canary, and independently re-observe both identities before countersign.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The countersigned Staging Recovery certificate is accepted only when provider-observed Worker provenance and fresh Gateway ingress identity remain exact-current for the same Staging source SHA and target fingerprint.
steps: Capture Cloudflare Worker deployment and version provenance through read-only provider APIs after the exact-SHA Staging deployment.
Expose only the sanitized Gateway ingress build identity and server-managed target fingerprint from Staging readiness.
Bind provider evidence to a fresh readiness response immediately before the local Recovery canary.
Re-observe Cloudflare Worker provenance and Gateway ingress identity independently in GitHub before countersign.
Fail closed on stale evidence, deployment drift, bundle mismatch, policy mismatch, target mismatch, or missing live observations.
assertions: Both staging and production impact are explicitly reviewed and live Staging certification remains required.
Production mutation remains forbidden and production_mutation_allowed is false.
Provider observation is read-only and does not perform Cloudflare, DNS, custom-domain, database, migration, grant, credential, or Production mutation.
Persisted evidence excludes provider credentials, auth digests, JTI values, signatures, replay tokens, and private keys.
The new Worker provider evidence script and this change declaration are registered exactly in Constitution.control_plane_paths and convergence.automation_control_paths.
Autonomous merge remains forbidden for the changed critical governance surface.
